context: Read the ADR 0005 G5 decision first and record which branch applies. Branch A, runbook only: extend docs/operations/hosted-credentials.md with a Provision once section giving the exact commands to mint a bounded capability-matched token and store it where the configured provider reads it, plus a Rotate section covering the periodic replacement and the verification step, and add no CLI subcommand. Branch B, first-party command: additionally add an explicit provisioning subcommand to src/todo_db/cli.py that is never invoked by any other command path and that writes only through the operator's chosen store. In both branches, update auth_remediation() and the CLI exit-4 text in src/todo_db/backends.py and src/todo_db/cli.py so the message names the procedure and the provider variable instead of asking the reader to inject something, and keep every string free of token values. Document rotation cadence against the ADR 0004 maximums rather than restating them.
description: The retrieval provider is useless until something puts a credential where the provider can find it, and today's exit-4 remediation says only 'inject a bounded credential and retry', which is the sentence that pushed the work onto the user. This item lands the one-time provisioning and periodic rotation procedure and makes the failure path name it. ADR 0005 G5 decides whether a first-party subcommand ships or the runbook documents the external commands, and either outcome must leave a concrete named procedure; 'the decision was documentation only' is not grounds to close this item without a procedure, because that is exactly how the injection half of the v0.4.2 plan disappeared.

anti_patterns.dont: Close this item with no procedure because G5 chose documentation over a subcommand
anti_patterns.instead: land the runbook procedure and the remediation text that names it
anti_patterns.why: the v0.4.2 cycle lost the injection half of the plan exactly this way, by narrowing scope with nothing re-homed

anti_patterns.dont: Have any normal command path call the provisioning routine on failure
anti_patterns.instead: keep it an explicit operator action reached only from the error message
anti_patterns.why: implicit remediation is the per-command minting behaviour ADR 0004 removed

anti_patterns.dont: Leave the exit-4 message as a generic instruction to inject a credential
anti_patterns.instead: name the provider variable and the provisioning procedure
anti_patterns.why: the generic message is what turned an architectural boundary into a user burden

anti_patterns.dont: Print, echo, or example a real token value in the runbook or tests
anti_patterns.instead: show command shapes and placeholder identifiers
anti_patterns.why: runbooks get copied into issues and transcripts

preserves.behavior: A G5 'runbook only' decision still ends with a named procedure and a remediation message that points at it.
Bearer values never appear in command output, examples, tests, tracker evidence, or the runbook.
Provisioning is explicit and interactive: no ordinary command, wrapper, doctor run, audit workflow, or CI job invokes it.
The ADR 0004 lifetime maximums and rotation ownership remain the single source of truth; this item references them rather than restating different numbers.
todo-db still never mints a token as part of a tracker operation, and a failed command never repairs its own credentials.
